messages:
acme_ops: We're seeing TLS handshake resets from our private inference nodes to model-hosted.redwood.ai after a security hardening window. Started ~2026-03-12 10:20 UTC. Streaming requests connect but drop mid-stream with RST. No app errors, just connection resets. Any pointers?

lee_support: hey @acme_ops — can you paste a short tcpdump from an affected pod/host + your SG/NACL rules? First guess is something blocking return traffic on high ports.

acme_ops: tcpdump from inference-01 (cut):
```
13:20:31.123456 IP 10.0.5.12.51234 > 34.210.100.55.443: Flags [S], seq 12345, win 64240, options [mss 1460], length 0
13:20:31.223789 IP 34.210.100.55.443 > 10.0.5.12.51234: Flags [R], seq 0, win 0, length 0
```
Client sends SYN from source port 51234 to dest 443, immediate RST from model-hosted IP. traceroute shows path via nat-gw-01. No TLS alert in app logs.

alex_oncall: do you have the NAT translation for that session? i.e. on nat-gw, what source port mapped? also paste the NACL outbound/inbound rules (rule numbers help).

acme_ops: NACLs on the private-subnet: 
```
Rule 100: ALLOW 443 inbound 0.0.0.0/0
Rule 110: DENY 1024-65535 outbound 0.0.0.0/0
Rule 200: ALLOW ephemeral-range inbound 1024-65535 10.0.0.0/16
```
we tightened rules during the hardening window. We thought locking outbound high ports was safe because SGs are stateful.

network_eng: This is the classic stateless NACL trap. NACLs evaluate inbound/outbound independently. If your outbound NACL denies 1024-65535, the response packets (server->client) that use high source ports won't be allowed back out, so you get RSTs or resets from the network. Fix options:
- Add an outbound ALLOW for 1024-65535 (rule < 110) for the NAT/subnet range
- Or rely on stateful SGs on the NAT instance/eni and avoid blocking ephemeral in the subnet NACL
- Also confirm NAT gateway isn't translating to an unexpected EIP that the model-hosted side blocks.

lee_support: quick repro checklist to give customers:
1) From a bastion in the same subnet: `curl -v https://model-hosted.redwood.ai/health` (if it works from bastion but fails from pod -> NACL/NAT path likely)
2) `sudo tcpdump -n -i any port 443` on the host while reproducing, capture SYN and response flags
3) paste NACL rules (both in and out) and SG attached to the NAT/gw and the inference host
4) if using IP allowlists upstream, confirm the NAT EIP matches the allowlist

acme_ops: ran the curl from bastion -> succeeds. From pod -> RST. Applied outbound allow for 1024-65535 on the subnet NACL (temporary) and retries: streaming sessions stay up and no more RST.

oncall-bot: Incident INC-7890 marked resolved by @lee_support :white_check_mark:

acme_ops: thanks everyone — lesson learned: subnet-level NACLs are stateless; tightening outbound ephemeral ports broke streaming. We'll update our infra hardening playbook and open a PR to make the NACL change explicit in the terraform module. :raised_hands:
